_comment: Template for your own labelled corpus. Copy to labels.json, point the paths at real projects, and label each one the way a knowledgeable reviewer would answer Apple's Social Media question — BEFORE you run the classifier against it. Labels written after seeing the output measure nothing.

_scale.yes: A reviewer would answer yes to Apple's Social Media question.
_scale.ambiguous: Genuinely undecidable without asking the developer. Scored correct only if the tool declines to commit — see validate.py.

_why_ambiguous_matters: If almost every app you label is trivially yes or no, you do not need a classifier — you need a one-page explainer. The size of the ambiguous band is the thing worth measuring.

apps.note: Public feed of user posts with likes, comments and a follower graph. Unambiguous.

Comments among invited members of a private group, no public discovery surface. Out of scope under Apple's reference-page definition ('visibly spreads content to many users'), arguably in scope under the 9 July 2026 news post that drops the clause.
Editorially curated content, favourites stored locally. No user-generated content at all.
Game Center leaderboards only. Apple-managed aliases, no feed of the app's own.
